24	# Architecture Spine — Cerne
25	
26	## Design Paradigm
27	
28	**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**
29	
30	- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
31	- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
32	- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
33	- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.
34	
35	```mermaid
36	flowchart TD
37	    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
38	        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
39	        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
40	        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
41	        P --> D
42	        DA --> D
43	    end
44	    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, design_tokens)"]
45	    Feature --> Core
46	    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
47	    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
48	```
49	
50	## Invariants & Rules
51	
52	### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)
53	
54	- **Binds:** all features
55	- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
56	- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.
57	
58	### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)
59	
60	- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
61	- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
62	- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.
63	
64	### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`
65	
66	- **Binds:** all
67	- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
68	- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature.
69	
70	### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`
71	
72	- **Binds:** the API client
73	- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
74	- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.
75	
76	### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy
77	
78	- **Binds:** every network call
79	- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
80	- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.
81	
82	### AD-6 — Cross-feature access only through a domain-layer port
83	
84	- **Binds:** RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
85	- **Prevents:** a feature reaching into another feature's `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
86	- **Rule:** the *owning* feature defines an abstract use case/port in its own `domain/` (e.g. `entries/domain` exposes `SaveEntryUseCase`) and registers the concrete implementation in its own DI registration function. A *consuming* feature (e.g. `chat`) only ever imports and injects that abstract type from the owning feature's `domain/` — never anything from its `data/` or `presentation/`.
87	
88	### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references
89	
90	- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
91	- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
92	- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.
93	
94	### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth
95	
96	- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
97	- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
98	- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream.
99	
100	### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue
101	
102	- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
103	- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
104	- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Read operations transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.
105	
106	### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)
107	
108	- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
109	- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
110	- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from `Entry.serverRevision` + `Entry.updatedAt` + the transient pending-write flag (AD-9). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).
111	
112	### AD-11 — Entry immutability
113	
114	- **Binds:** the entries feature
115	- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
116	- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.
117	
118	### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`
119	
120	- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02 or RF07
121	- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
122	- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`) and RF07's composite auth × sync × data state each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`.
123	
124	### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`
125	
126	- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
127	- **Prevents:** RF08 reinventing its own failure-isolation wrapper (or importing RF10's feature-local one), producing two incompatible "never block the caller on failure" implementations.
128	- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.
129	
130	## Consistency Conventions
131	
132	| Concern | Convention |
133	| --- | --- |
134	| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
135	| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
136	| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
137	| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |
138	| Network envelope | one `ApiClient`/URL-builder + one header interceptor (AD-5); no feature constructs a request URL or header set itself |
139	| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |

You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When not to use

If the target is already known, use the direct tool: Read for a known path, `grep` via the Bash tool for a specific symbol or string. Reserve this tool for open-ended questions that span the codebase, or tasks that match an available agent type.

## Usage notes

- Always include a short description summarizing what the agent will do
- When the agent is done, its final report is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- Agents run in the background by default. When an agent runs in the background, you will be automatically notified when it completes — do NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress. Continue with other work or respond to the user instead.
- **Foreground vs background**: Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — e.g., a research agent whose finding gates the edit you're about to make. Otherwise let it run in the background (the default) — this includes fire-and-forget work, independent investigations, and anything where the user might hand you something else in the meantime. Wanting the result "next" is not enough on its own.
- **Don't race**: after launching a background agent, you know nothing about its results. Never fabricate or predict them in any format — not as prose, summary, or structured output. The completion notification arrives in a later turn; it is never something you write yourself. If the user asks before it lands, say the agent is still running — give status, not a guess.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field — that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs, so the prompt must be self-contained.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tool access are set in its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter, or the SDK `agents` option).
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since a fresh agent is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Agent tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a build-validator agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.
- With `isolation: "worktree"`, the worktree is automatically cleaned up if the agent makes no changes; otherwise the path and branch are returned in the result.

## Writing the prompt

Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room — it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question — prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

Terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

Example usage:

<example>
user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"
assistant: <thinking>A survey question across git state, tests, and config. I'll delegate it and ask for a short report so the raw command output stays out of my context.</thinking>
Agent({
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",
  prompt: "Audit what's left before this branch can ship. Check: uncommitted changes, commits ahead of main, whether tests exist, whether the GrowthBook gate is wired up, whether CI-relevant files changed. Report a punch list — done vs. missing. Under 200 words."
})
assistant: Ship-readiness audit running in the background.
<commentary>
The prompt is self-contained: it states the goal, lists what to check, and caps the response length. The agent runs in the background (the default), so the turn ends here — nothing about its findings is known yet. The report arrives in a SEPARATE turn, as a completion notification from outside; it is never something you write yourself.
</commentary>
[later turn — notification arrives as user message]
assistant: Audit's back. Three blockers: no tests for the new prompt path, GrowthBook gate wired but not in build_flags.yaml, and one uncommitted file.
</example>

<example>
user: "so is the gate wired up or not"
<commentary>
User asks mid-wait. The audit was launched to answer exactly this, and it hasn't returned. Give status, not a fabricated result.
</commentary>
assistant: Still waiting on the audit — that's one of the things it's checking. Should land shortly.
</example>

<example>
user: "Can you get a second opinion on whether this migration is safe?"
assistant: <thinking>I'll ask the code-reviewer agent — it won't see my analysis, so it can give an independent read.</thinking>
Agent({
  description: "Independent migration review",
  subagent_type: "code-reviewer",
  prompt: "Review migration 0042_user_schema.sql for safety. Context: we're adding a NOT NULL column to a 50M-row table. Existing rows get a backfill default. I want a second opinion on whether the backfill approach is safe under concurrent writes — I've checked locking behavior but want independent verification. Report: is this safe, and if not, what specifically breaks?"
})
<commentary>
The agent starts with no context from this conversation, so the prompt briefs it: what to assess, the relevant background, and what form the answer should take.
</commentary>
</example>

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or for an HTML or Markdown page to view or share. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save. A page declares these through the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of this would make the page more useful, Claude must load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code.** Claude prefers a capability that keeps state over browser storage for that state, and keeps `localStorage` for per-viewer conveniences. Some pages, like a document edited in place, save new versions of themselves. Such a save reaches this session like any other republish, as a notice on a watched artifact or a conflict on Claude's next publish, and Claude then re-reads the page, merges the changes and republishes.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. The one exception is a workshop document from the `workshop` skill, which carries its own design: there Claude skips `artifact-design` and loads `artifact-diagramming` for a template page's diagrams. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com or cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ (the skill has the full list) and stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- git status → "Show working tree status"

- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). # Adversarial Review — Architecture Spine (Cerne)

**Verdict: real holes.** Four of the six attack pairs below produce concrete, letter-compliant-yet-incompatible builds; two are already closed (confirmed, with evidence) and are recorded so a future reviewer doesn't re-raise them.

---

## 1. RF01 (capture) vs RF07 (entries) — two owners of the `Entry` entity and `POST /entries`

**Scenario.** Delivery order is `F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → …`. RF01's own acceptance criteria ("Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`)") makes RF01 — not RF07 — the first build unit that must create entries, and it is built two full units *before* `features/entries/` exists. Yet AD-6's example ("`entries/domain` exposes `SaveEntryUseCase`") and the Structural Seed both attribute `features/entries/` and its `SaveEntryUseCase` to **RF06/RF07**. The Capability → Architecture Map makes it worse: RF01's row lists only `AD-1, AD-2, AD-9` as governing ADs — AD-6 (cross-feature port) and AD-11 (entry create/read only) are never cited against RF01 at all.

A session building RF01 to the letter has no signal that it must scaffold `features/entries/domain/` first; the obvious, AD-1/AD-2/AD-9-compliant move is to build a `createEntry` call straight inside `features/capture/data` (own repository, own `Entry`-shaped DTO, own hive_ce box) because nothing tells it `features/entries/` is the *owning* feature for an entity capture is only using. Two units later, the RF07 session reads the Structural Seed, sees "`entries/` — RF06, RF07 … exposes `SaveEntryUseCase` (AD-6)," and — also fully AD-compliant — builds its *own* `EntriesRepository`/`Entry` model/hive_ce box from scratch for listing. Both are AD-1/AD-2/AD-6-literal. The result: two `Entry` models, two cache boxes, two repository owners of the same backend resource, and capture's writes never reach whatever cache/sync-badge state (AD-10) RF07 built, because RF07 didn't know capture already wrote one.

**Real or closed?** Real — and the most severe of the six; it's a direct "two owners of one entity" collision, worsened by the Capability Map actively omitting the AD-6 link on RF01's row.

**Proposed fix.** Tighten AD-6 (or add AD-6a): *"`features/entries/` — including `Entry`, `EntriesRepository` (create + read), and `SaveEntryUseCase` — is scaffolded at RF01 time, not RF07 time, because RF01's own AC requires `POST /entries`. RF01 is the first consumer of `SaveEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository.createEntry`; RF07 only adds the read/list/timeline methods to that already-existing repository. RF01's row in the Capability → Architecture Map must cite AD-6 and AD-11."* Also correct the Capability Map row for RF01 to add `AD-6, AD-11` and fix the Structural Seed comment on `entries/` to read `RF01, RF06, RF07`.

---

## 2. F000 (auth/session) vs RF03 (vault) — two independent navigation gates, one `go_router`

**Scenario.** F000 owns "base nav" and wires `go_router`'s redirect against the single `SessionStatus` stream (AD-8: authenticated/unauthenticated/expired → login redirect). RF03 (vault: biometric/PIN, 5-minute background timeout) is explicitly "local-only, zero `Either` plumbing" per the Capability Map, and is a *second*, independent gate: a valid Supabase session can still be sitting behind a locked vault after backgrounding. `go_router`'s top-level `redirect` callback is singular — composing two independent gating conditions onto it normally requires merging listenables (`Listenable.merge`) or chaining redirect logic. No AD says this.

F000, built first, has no reason to anticipate a second gate and may wire `redirect` as a plain closure over `SessionStatus` with no extension point. RF03, built right after and in a separate session with no visibility into F000's actual router wiring beyond what the spine documents (which says nothing about redirect composition), must now either (a) add a second competing `redirect` to the same `GoRouter` instance — which silently overrides or race-conditions with F000's — or (b) bypass routing entirely and gate via a global overlay/`builder`. Either choice is AD-8-compliant to the letter (AD-8 only pins *session* status, not vault-lock status, as the single source of truth) and neither is wrong per the ADs as written — but the two mechanisms were never required to compose, so whichever the RF03 session picks, F000 was never told to leave room for it.

**Real or closed?** Real. AD-8 binds F000's redirect and RF07's composite state to `SessionStatus`, but never mentions RF03's vault-lock state at all, and no other AD governs multi-gate composition on the router.

**Proposed fix.** New AD: *"App-level navigation gating is a single composed function, not one gate per feature. `core/` (or `features/auth/`) exposes one `Listenable`/stream that merges `SessionStatus` (AD-8) with the vault feature's lock state; `go_router`'s top-level `redirect` reads only that merged signal. RF03 does not add a second `redirect` callback or a parallel navigation-interception mechanism — it registers its lock state into the merge point F000 leaves for it."*

---

## 3. RF08 (proactive insights) vs RF10 (save-to-journal) — `isolatedSideEffect`'s signature pins types, not await semantics

**Scenario.** AD-13 fixes `isolatedSideEffect`'s signature (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`) and says it "ships with RF10 (first consumer)," with RF08 reusing it. But every repository method is *already* non-throwing by AD-2 (`Either` at the boundary) — so the signature alone doesn't say what `isolatedSideEffect` adds. The two plausible, both letter-compliant, implementations diverge exactly on the property AD-13 was written to standardize:

- RF10's save-to-journal only needs "never let a failed save crash the chat screen, just show a failed sync badge" — a session building this first could reasonably implement `isolatedSideEffect` as a synchronous `try/await` wrapper that still *awaits* the inner future before returning, just without rethrowing. That satisfies "never throws past itself" and every acceptance criterion RF10 has.
- RF08's proactive insight generation is described as a side channel that must not block the chat send/receive flow while the (potentially slow, Claude-backed) insight call runs. That needs genuine fire-and-forget semantics — kick off the future, return/continue immediately, surface the `Either` asynchronously later (e.g., via a stream) — not an awaited wrapper.

Both are "`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`"-shaped. Nothing in AD-13 says whether the helper awaits before returning or detaches. If RF10 builds (and ships, per AD-13) the awaited version, RF08 either misuses it (blocking insight generation on the chat flow after all — the exact bug AD-13 exists to prevent) or has to build a second, incompatible variant anyway — defeating "RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import," which only works if the one implementation already does what RF08 needs.

**Real or closed?** Real. AD-13 closes "two different failure-isolation wrappers" at the type level but not at the concurrency-semantics level, which is the part that actually matters for RF08.

**Proposed fix.** Tighten AD-13: *"`isolatedSideEffect` does not await its inner future before returning to the caller; it schedules the future, returns immediately (`Future<Either<Failure,T>>` that completes independently of the caller's control flow), and never couples the caller's continuation to the side effect's completion. Any consumer that needs the resolved `Either` (e.g., to update a sync badge) subscribes to it as a separate, non-blocking completion — never by awaiting the wrapper inline in the main request path."*

---

## 4. RF04 (chat/RAG) vs RF08 (proactive insight) — no AD names RF04's state shape, so RF08 can't be sure what it's composing onto

**Scenario.** AD-12 is explicit that `Resource<T>` is used only for single-source/single-fetch screens, and explicitly carves out RF02 (capture state machine) and RF07 (composite auth×sync×data state) as needing their own sealed state. RF06 and RF09 are explicitly named as `Resource<T>` users. **RF04 (chat, with its SSE message stream and "AI status indicator") is named in neither list.** A chat SSE stream is multi-event and long-lived — arguably it should be excluded from `Resource<T>` the same way RF02 is, but AD-12's text doesn't say so, so an RF04 session reading AD-12 literally ("used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle") could defensibly go either way: treat the whole chat screen as one `Resource<T>` fetch (wrong fit, but not explicitly forbidden) or build a bespoke sealed class (not explicitly required either).

RF08, built immediately after RF04 and explicitly needing to overlay a proactive-insight signal onto the same chat screen without a BLoC-to-BLoC reference (AD-7), has to compose its insight stream with whatever RF04 chose. If RF04 picked `Resource<T>`'s 4-state enum for the whole screen, there is no slot for "insight arrived" that doesn't collide with `data`/`loading` for the primary message stream — RF08 then has no AD-sanctioned shape to merge into, and is forced into a workaround (e.g., a second parallel `Resource<T>` read by the widget tree) that AD-12 never anticipated and that two independently-built sessions would not converge on the same way.

**Real or closed?** Real, though milder than #1–#3 — it's an omission (RF04 missing from AD-12's named list) rather than a direct contradiction.

**Proposed fix.** Extend AD-12's rule to explicitly name RF04: *"RF04's chat/RAG screen (SSE message stream + AI status indicator) defines its own sealed state class, like RF02 and RF07, not `Resource<T>` — multi-event streams are categorically excluded from `Resource<T>`, not just the two named screens. RF08's proactive-insight signal is injected into RF04's chat BLoC as an additional domain-layer stream the BLoC listens to independently (per AD-7), not as a new enum case retrofitted onto RF04's existing state after the fact."*

---

## 5. RF06 (semantic search) vs `core/cache` (AD-9) — offline fallback semantics for search are undefined, and requirements.md itself is split

**Scenario.** AD-9 states a blanket rule: "Read operations transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache." `GET /entries/search` is a read (`entries.search`, `bearerAuth`, `x-cerne-function: entries-search`). But requirements.md is internally inconsistent about what that means for *search* specifically: §6's RF06 AC says "Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection… offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing" (implying a cache-backed, degraded-but-present offline experience), while §13's error-taxonomy table lists `NETWORK_OFFLINE` as "action blocked (see RF04/**RF06**)" (implying search is simply blocked offline, like a write).

The spine never resolves this contradiction — AD-9 just repeats the generic "reads fall back to cache" rule without addressing that semantic search has no meaningful local fallback (there's no on-device embedding index; the cache only holds previously-*fetched* entries, not a search index). Two sessions building RF06 independently, both reading AD-9 literally, could land on:
- **Session A:** search is a "read," so it must fall back to cache like everything else — implemented as: on `NetworkOffline`, silently re-filter the last-fetched *unfiltered* entries list by a naive substring match and show that as "results," because that's the only thing the cache actually contains.
- **Session B:** search inherently requires a live embedding call it cannot serve from cache, so it should behave like a write under AD-9 — return `Either.left(NetworkOffline)` immediately, no cache attempt, matching the error-taxonomy table.

Both comply with AD-9's text; they produce opposite UX (silently-different "results" vs. an explicit blocked-action error), and whichever a given session picks, nothing in the spine would flag it as wrong — yet RF06's own AC explicitly anticipates this exact ambiguity.

**Real or closed?** Real — and already flagged as fuzzy by requirements.md itself, which makes it worse that the spine's AD-9 doesn't resolve it (the Deferred section even calls out the search+filter combination as open, but not this offline-semantics split).

**Proposed fix.** Tighten AD-9: *"AD-9's cache-fallback rule applies only to reads that return previously-synced records as-is (`entries.list`, `entries.get`, `chat.sessions.list`, `chat.messages.list`). Reads that require a live server-side computation with no on-device equivalent — `entries.search` (semantic embedding) foremost — are offline-blocked exactly like writes: `NetworkOffline` is returned immediately, with no cache-filtered substitute ever presented as 'results.' RF06's screen falls back only to redisplaying its own last-successful search result set (frozen, with an explicit stale/offline indicator), never to live-filtering the general entries cache."*

---

## 6. (Checked, not real) RF09 (dashboard) vs RF07 (entries/timeline) — entry aggregation

**Scenario considered.** RF09's dashboard needs period aggregates and a narrative; RF07 already owns the entries timeline/cache. The adversarial hypothesis was that RF09 would need to reach into `features/entries/` (via an AD-6 port) to compute aggregates client-side from the same entries RF07 already fetched/cached, risking a second, divergent aggregation path.

**Why it's not real.** Verified against `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`: `GET /dashboard/aggregate` (`dashboard-aggregate-get`) returns fully server-computed `buckets`/`totals` keyed by date and source, and `GET /dashboard/narrative` (`dashboard-narrative-get`) returns a server-generated `text`/`generatedAt` pair — neither response includes entry IDs or any field referencing the `Entry` entity. RF09 never needs to touch `features/entries/` at all; it talks to its own backend endpoints directly, exactly as AD-12 already assumes (RF09 named as a `Resource<T>`-eligible, single-fetch screen for each of the two calls). AD-6's cross-feature-port rule simply isn't triggered here. No fix needed; recorded so a future reviewer doesn't re-raise this pair without checking the contract first.

---

## Summary of proposed spine changes

| # | Pair | Status | Fix target |
| - | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | RF01 vs RF07 (`Entry` ownership) | Real (severe) | Tighten AD-6 + fix Capability Map row for RF01 + fix Structural Seed `entries/` comment |
| 2 | F000 vs RF03 (nav gates) | Real | New AD on composed `go_router` redirect/listenable |
| 3 | RF08 vs RF10 (`isolatedSideEffect`) | Real | Tighten AD-13 to pin non-blocking/detached scheduling semantics |
| 4 | RF04 vs RF08 (chat state shape) | Real | Extend AD-12 to name RF04 explicitly and exclude multi-event streams generally |
| 5 | RF06 vs AD-9 (search offline semantics) | Real | Tighten AD-9 to scope cache-fallback to as-is reads only; search is offline-blocked |
| 6 | RF09 vs RF07 (entry aggregation) | Not real (confirmed via contract) | None |

F000, built first, has no reason to anticipate a second gate and may wire `redirect` as a plain closure over `SessionStatus` with no extension point. RF03, built right after and in a separate session with no visibility into F000's actual router wiring beyond what the spine documents (which says nothing about redirect composition), must now either (a) add a second competing `redirect` to the same `GoRouter` instance — which silently overrides or race-conditions with F000's — or (b) bypass routing entirely and gate via a global overlay/`builder`. Either choice is AD-8-compliant to the letter (AD-8 only pins *session* status, not vault-lock status, as the single source of truth) and neither is wrong per the ADs as written — but the two mechanisms were never required to compose, so whichever the RF03 session picks, F000 was never told to leave room for it.

**Real or closed?** Real. AD-8 binds F000's redirect and RF07's composite state to `SessionStatus`, but never mentions RF03's vault-lock state at all, and no other AD governs multi-gate composition on the router.

**Proposed fix.** New AD: *"App-level navigation gating is a single composed function, not one gate per feature. `core/` (or `features/auth/`) exposes one `Listenable`/stream that merges `SessionStatus` (AD-8) with the vault feature's lock state; `go_router`'s top-level `redirect` reads only that merged signal. ---

## 3. RF08 (proactive insights) vs RF10 (save-to-journal) — `isolatedSideEffect`'s signature pins types, not await semantics

**Scenario.** AD-13 fixes `isolatedSideEffect`'s signature (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`) and says it "ships with RF10 (first consumer)," with RF08 reusing it. - RF10's save-to-journal only needs "never let a failed save crash the chat screen, just show a failed sync badge" — a session building this first could reasonably implement `isolatedSideEffect` as a synchronous `try/await` wrapper that still *awaits* the inner future before returning, just without rethrowing. If RF04 picked `Resource<T>`'s 4-state enum for the whole screen, there is no slot for "insight arrived" that doesn't collide with `data`/`loading` for the primary message stream — RF08 then has no AD-sanctioned shape to merge into, and is forced into a workaround (e.g., a second parallel `Resource<T>` read by the widget tree) that AD-12 never anticipated and that two independently-built sessions would not converge on the same way.

**Real or closed?** Real, though milder than #1–#3 — it's an omission (RF04 missing from AD-12's named list) rather than a direct contradiction.

**Proposed fix.** Extend AD-12's rule to explicitly name RF04: *"RF04's chat/RAG screen (SSE message stream + AI status indicator) defines its own sealed state class, like RF02 and RF07, not `Resource<T>` — multi-event streams are categorically excluded from `Resource<T>`, not just the two named screens. ## 5. RF06 (semantic search) vs `core/cache` (AD-9) — offline fallback semantics for search are undefined, and requirements.md itself is split

- **Session B:** search inherently requires a live embedding call it cannot serve from cache, so it should behave like a write under AD-9 — return `Either.left(NetworkOffline)` immediately, no cache attempt, matching the error-taxonomy table.

**Real or closed?** Real — and already flagged as fuzzy by requirements.md itself, which makes it worse that the spine's AD-9 doesn't resolve it (the Deferred section even calls out the search+filter combination as open, but not this offline-semantics split).

**Proposed fix.** Tighten AD-9: *"AD-9's cache-fallback rule applies only to reads that return previously-synced records as-is (`entries.list`, `entries.get`, `chat.sessions.list`, `chat.messages.list`). Reads that require a live server-side computation with no on-device equivalent — `entries.search` (semantic embedding) foremost — are offline-blocked exactly like writes: `NetworkOffline` is returned immediately, with no cache-filtered substitute ever presented as 'results.' RF06's screen falls back only to redisplaying its own last-successful search result set (frozen, with an explicit stale/offline indicator), never to live-filtering the general entries cache."*

AD-6's cross-feature-port rule simply isn't triggered here. No fix needed; recorded so a future reviewer doesn't re-raise this pair without checking the contract first.
